paper_metadata.title: Efficient State Preparation for Quantum Amplitude Estimation

summary: The paper presents gate-based QAE state-preparation techniques and demonstrates them on two IBM Q Ourense hardware experiments for numerical integration with 2 and 3 discretization qubits, using 8192 shots per circuit and MLAE, plus a noiseless 8-qubit simulation for Heston-model option pricing. It reports Spin-Echo optimization reducing CNOT counts substantially and gives a simulated Heston payoff probability of 0.1185 for measuring |1111>, but it does not show a practical classical-vs-quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Real-hardware numerical integration experiment estimating integrals of sin^2(pi x) using QAE/MLAE with 1 and 2 discretization qubits, comparing left/right Riemann, midpoint, and Simpson quadrature rules, and using Spin-Echo circuit optimization.

hyperparameters.kmax: varied; up to 16 for 2-qubit case and up to 2 for 3-qubit case in the main hardware study

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n discretization qubits encode 2^n grid points; objective function g(x)=sin^2(pi x) is loaded via controlled Ry rotations; good state flagged by ancilla qubit(s) in |1>
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate integral \int_0^y sin^2(pi x) dx via QAE/MLAE; equivalently estimate E[g(X)] for discretized X

problem_instance.description: Numerical integration of sin^2(pi x) over [0,y] for y in [0,1], evaluated for multiple y values; discretization with 1 and 2 qubits in the main hardware study

dataset_specification.description: Analytic test function sin^2(pi x) on interval [0,1]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize [0,y] using left/right Riemann, midpoint, or Simpson grid points; scale result by y for y<1
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MLAE over repeated circuit executions; 8192 shots per circuit; compare estimated values and absolute errors against analytic integral

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: readout error mitigation; noisy-gate insertion with Richardson extrapolation

implementation_details.mitigation_details: Readout calibration matrix over all basis states; CNOT noise amplified by replacing each CNOT with 3 and 5 CNOTs, then quadratic extrapolation to zero-noise limit
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Pre-compute rotation angles for the discretized function values; choose k values for MLAE
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Combine measurement outcomes with MLAE; apply readout correction and zero-noise extrapolation

speedup_claims.conditions: for QAE/MLAE state preparation when the problem is efficiently loadable
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that practical performance is limited by circuit depth and noise; the quadratic rate is the ideal QAE scaling.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Small-scale QPU demonstration on IBM Q Ourense with 2 discretization qubits; 8192 shots per circuit; MLAE with k up to 16 in the 2-qubit case.
limiting_factors: Only toy-scale integrals over sin^2(pi x)
Noise and CNOT overhead on real hardware
Quadratic speedup only, which Hoefler-style constant-factor analysis disfavors on NISQ hardware
State-preparation and circuit-depth growth with k

notes: The paper reports 2-qubit and 3-qubit hardware experiments; this entry summarizes the main 2-qubit numerical-integration experiment and uses num_qubits=2 as the smallest reported hardware configuration. Circuit depth is not given as a single explicit depth number; only CNOT counts and k-dependent circuit growth are reported, so circuit_depth is left null/inferred only at a qualitative level.
The paper reports hardware results and error trends, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical numerical integration.

hyperparameters.kmax: up to 2 in the main 3-qubit hardware study

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate integral \int_0^y sin^2(pi x) dx via QAE/MLAE

problem_instance.description: Numerical integration of sin^2(pi x) over [0,y] for y in [0,1], evaluated on 3-qubit discretization; hardware connectivity compared between all-to-all and linear layouts

dataset_specification.description: Analytic test function sin^2(pi x) on interval [0,1]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize [0,y] using left/right Riemann, midpoint, or Simpson grid points; scale result by y for y<1
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MLAE over repeated circuit executions; 8192 shots per circuit; compare estimated values and absolute errors against analytic integral

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: readout error mitigation; noisy-gate insertion with Richardson extrapolation

experiments.description: Simulation study for pricing a European call option under the Heston stochastic volatility model using QAE-style state preparation and amplitude estimation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Four state qubits discretize the stochastic process variables (nu1, S1, S2) and four ancilla qubits flag the transition probabilities and payoff; probabilities loaded via controlled rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[max(S_T - K, 0)] for a European call option under the Heston model

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under the Heston model with two time steps (t=0,1,2) and discretized volatility/stock-price paths

dataset_specification.description: Parameters K=1, delta_t=1, T=2, nu0=1, S0=1, kappa=1, theta=1, xi=0.5, mu=1, rho=0; discretize nu1, S1, S2 on small grids

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Convert continuous transition PDFs to discrete interval probabilities using midpoint intervals around grid points; normalize payoff g(S2)=max(S2-K,0) by dividing by 2
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation only; evaluate probability of measuring |1111> and compare to marginal distribution-based reference value 0.1185

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Pre-compute transition probabilities for the discretized Heston model and corresponding controlled-rotation angles
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute the probability of measuring |1111> from simulation and compare with the analytically derived marginal distribution

speedup_claims.conditions: for estimating the expected payoff under the Heston model using QAE-style state preparation with efficiently computable transition probabilities
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a simulation study only; no hardware execution is reported for the Heston model.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speed-up in QAE estimation error; state preparation scales polynomially in the number of discretized variables when transition probabilities are efficiently computable
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo baseline scales as O(1/sqrt(M)) for estimation error

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware execution; noiseless simulation of an 8-qubit Heston-model state-preparation circuit with probability of |1111> reported as 0.1185.
limiting_factors: Quadratic QAE scaling without demonstrated end-to-end advantage

notes: The paper states the circuit uses four state qubits and four ancilla qubits, totaling eight qubits. It does not report a total depth or gate counts for the Heston simulation circuit.
The paper reports a simulated option-pricing construction and the probability 0.1185 for measuring |1111>, but does not claim or demonstrate practical advantage.
